sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: 3.1 The Need for Smaller Units Sonu’s mother was fixing a toy.
sections.source_evidence: 3.1 The Need for Smaller Units Sonu’s mother was fixing a toy.

sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: She was trying to join two pieces with the help of a screw.
sections.source_evidence: She was trying to join two pieces with the help of a screw.

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: Sonu was watching his mother with great curiosity.
sections.source_evidence: Sonu was watching his mother with great curiosity.

sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: His mother was unable to join the pieces.
sections.source_evidence: His mother was unable to join the pieces.

sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: His mother said that the screw was not of the right size.
sections.source_evidence: His mother said that the screw was not of the right size.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: She brought another screw from the box and was able to fix the toy.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: But when he observed them closely, he saw they were of slightly different lengths.

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: Sonu was fascinated by how such a small difference in lengths could matter so much.
sections.source_evidence: Sonu was fascinated by how such a small difference in lengths could matter so much.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: He was curious to know the difference in lengths.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: He was also curious to know how little the difference was because the screws looked nearly the same.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: In the following figure, screws are placed above a scale.

sections.content: Measure them and write their length in the space provided.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: A Peek Beyond the Point Which scale helped you measure the length of the screws accurately?

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: What is the meaning of 2 7 10 cm (the length of the first screw)?

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: As seen on the ruler, the unit length between two consecutive numbers is divided into 10 equal parts.
sections.source_evidence: As seen on the ruler, the unit length between two consecutive numbers is divided into 10 equal parts.

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: To get the length 2 7 10 cm, we go from 0 to 2 and then take seven parts of 1 10.
sections.source_evidence: To get the length 2 7 10 cm, we go from 0 to 2 and then take seven parts of 1 10.

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: The length of the screw is 2 cm and 7 10 cm.

sections.heading: Learning Point 18
sections.content: Similarly, we can make sense of the length 3 2 10 cm.

sections.heading: Learning Point 19
sections.content: We read 2 7 10 cm as two and seven-tenth centimeters, and 3 2 10 cm as three and two-tenth centimeters.

sections.heading: Learning Point 20
sections.content: Can you explain why the unit was divided into smaller parts to measure the screws?
